sop-from-memo.output:
Water Heater Swap

You will need
  Water shut-off at main
  Breaker for water heater
  Garden hose from van
  Floor drain nearby
  New water heater (size UNKNOWN — ASK OWNER)
  New flex lines (quantity UNKNOWN — ASK OWNER)
  Camera or phone for photo
  Closest faucet for air bleed

Steps

1. Shut the water at the main valve — do not rely on the small valve on the heater itself.

2. Turn off the breaker for the water heater at the electrical panel.

3. Attach the garden hose from the van to the drain port on the heater and run it to the floor drain. Open the drain and let the tank empty completely.

4. Disconnect the old water lines and flex lines from the heater.

5. Remove the old heater and place the new one in the same location.

6. Install new flex lines on both the hot and cold sides — use new ones every time, even if the old ones appear undamaged.

7. Fill the new heater by turning the main water valve back on.

8. Bleed air from the system by opening the faucet closest to the heater and letting water run until it flows steady with no sputters.

9. Turn the breaker back on to power the heater.

10. Wait 20 minutes, then check all connections and the floor around the heater for leaks.

11. Take a photo of the installed heater and any connections for the file.

Done looks like
  Water off at main, breaker off, heater fully drained into floor drain
  Old heater removed, new heater in place, new flex lines installed on both sides
  Heater filled, air bled at closest faucet, breaker on, no water flowing
  No leaks visible after 20 minutes
  Photo in file

Common mistakes
  Forgetting the expansion tank when a check valve is installed on the main — ASK OWNER whether this job has a check valve and whether an expansion tank is needed before you start.
  Checking for leaks at 2 minutes instead of 20 — small leaks take time to show. Wait the full 20 minutes.
  Reusing old flex lines to save time — always install new ones. Old lines can split under pressure.
